RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r1.claim: After completing the proofs of God's oneness and resurrection, God swears another oath.
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r1.anchor: لما فرغ من دليل التوحيد ، والمعاد أقسم قسما آخر

RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r2.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains al-rajʿ as rain because it comes back repeatedly; Rāzī says this is a metaphorical name, not the word's literal designation.
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج الرجع المطر لأنه يجيء ويتكرر

RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r3.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r3.claim: Al-Qaffāl compares recurring rain to the repeated return of sound in an echo.
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r3.anchor: قال القفال : كأنه من ترجيع الصوت وهو إعادته ووصل الحروف به

RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r4.claim: Another proposed metaphor reflects the Arabs' belief that clouds carry water from the earth's seas and return it to the land.
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r4.anchor: أن العرب كانوا يزعمون أن السحاب يحمل الماء من بحار الأرض ثم يرجعه إلى الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r5.claim: The name may be an optimistic wish that rain will return.
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r5.anchor: أنهم أرادوا التفاؤل فسموه رجعا ليرجع

RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r6.claim: It may also refer to rain's recurrence every year.
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r6.anchor: أن المطر يرجع في كل عام

RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the sky as bringing rain again and again.
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { والسماء ذات الرجع } أي ذات المطر يرجع لمطر بعد مطر

RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r8.claim: Another interpretation is that the sky repeatedly supplies its benefits over time.
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r8.anchor: رجع السماء إعطاء الخير الذي يكون من جهتها حالا بعد حال

RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says the sky returns the sun and moon after they set.
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن زيد : هو أنها ترد وترجع شمسها وقمرها بعد مغيبهما

RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r10.claim: Rāzī prefers the first interpretation, rain.

RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r15.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r15.claim: The oath turns from animal creation to plant creation: sky is like a father and earth like a mother, both sustaining worldly life through repeated rain and growth.
RAZI-FULL:v31p120#2/r15.anchor: فالسماء ذات الرجع كالأب ، والأرض ذات الصدع كالأم وكلاهما من النعم العظام

STUDYQURAN:86:11/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r1.claim: The seasonal cycles and vegetation growth are signs of God's power to resurrect, paralleling the emergence of humans from base fluid in verses 6–8.
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r1.anchor: These verses refer to the cycles of the seasons and the growing of vegetation as signs that God can resurrect as He wills

STUDYQURAN:86:11/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r2.claim: In reference to heaven, rajʿ, or resurgence, refers to rains that return periodically.
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r2.anchor: refers to the rains that return periodically

STUDYQURAN:86:11/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r3.speaker: IK, Ṭ, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r3.claim: These commentators interpret the resurgent sky as rain or the clouds that bring rain.
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r3.anchor: Thus most interpret the resurgent sky as a reference to rain or to the clouds that bring rain (IK, Ṭ, Ṭs).

STUDYQURAN:86:11/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r4.claim: Another reported interpretation takes the resurgent sky as the continual return of the sun, moon, and other celestial bodies.
STUDYQURAN:86:11/r4.anchor: Others interpret it as a reference to the continual return of the sun, the moon, and other celestial bodies (Ṭ).

TAB-FULL:v24p302/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī understands the sky as returning with clouds and people's provisions each year.
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r1.anchor: ترجع بالغيوم وأرزاق العباد كل عام

TAB-FULL:v24p302/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r2.claim: He cites al-Mutanakhil's sword verse as poetic evidence for the Arabic usage of al-rajʿ.
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r2.anchor: ومنه قول المتنخل في صفة سيف

TAB-FULL:v24p302/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the sky's return as clouds containing rain.
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r3.anchor: عن خصيف، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس

TAB-FULL:v24p302/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains al-rajʿ as rainfall and provision returning each year.
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r4.anchor: يعني بالرجع: القطر والرزق كل عام

TAB-FULL:v24p302/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the sky returns people's provisions every year.

TAB-FULL:v24p302/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r6.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r6.claim: Ikrima, when asked about the phrase, says it returns with rain.
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r6.anchor: قال أبو رجاء: سئل عنها عكرمة، فقال: رجعت بالمطر

TAB-FULL:v24p302/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r7.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r7.claim: Mujāhid explains it as clouds that rain and then return with rain.
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r7.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد

TAB-FULL:v24p302/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r8.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r8.claim: Qatāda says the sky returns people's provisions each year; without this, people and livestock would perish, and he also glosses it as annual rain.

TAB-FULL:v24p302/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r9.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r9.anchor: حدثت عن الحسين، قال: سمعت أبا معاذ

TAB-FULL:v24p302/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r10.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r10.claim: Other interpreters take the sky's return to refer to the sun and moon setting and rising.
TAB-FULL:v24p302/r10.anchor: وقال آخرون: يعني بذلك: أن شمسها وقمرها يغيب ويطلع

TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r1.claim: The oath invokes changing sky and earth while the sworn-to speech is unchanging, grounded in the fixed reality of its ta'wil, which the tafsir will explain later.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#14/r1.anchor: انظر إلى موضع القسم بالسماء والأرض المتغيرتين والمعنى المقسم به في عدم تغيره واتكائه على حقيقة ثابتة هي تأويله

TABATABAI:86:10-17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r2.claim: The sky’s return is its observable course: stars rise after setting and set after rising.
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r2.anchor: والمراد بكون السماء ذات رجع ما يظهر للحس من سيرها بطلوع الكواكب بعد غروبها وغروبها بعد طلوعها

TABATABAI:86:10-17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r3.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r3.claim: An unnamed interpretation takes the sky’s “return” to mean rainfall.
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r3.anchor: وقيل رجعها إمطارها، والمراد بكون الأرض ذات صدع

TABATABAI:86:10-17/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r5.claim: The paired oaths confirm resurrection and return to God; the sky and earth imagery aptly fits return after death and emergence from graves.
TABATABAI:86:10-17/r5.anchor: إقسام بعد إقسام لتأكيد أمر القيامة والرجوع إلى الله

TABATABAI:86:10-13/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:86:10-13/r5.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:86:10-13/r5.claim: Al-Qummī interprets the sky’s “return” as rain.
TABATABAI:86:10-13/r5.anchor: وفيه في قوله تعالى { والسماء ذات الرجع } قال ذات المطر

TABRISI:86:9-17/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:9-17/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:86:9-17/r9.claim: The commentator presents this as another oath, reinforcing the reality of the Resurrection.
TABRISI:86:9-17/r9.anchor: ثم ذكر سبحانه قسما آخر تأكيدا لأمر القيامة

TABRISI:86:9-17/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:9-17/r10.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:86:9-17/r10.claim: Most commentators take the sky's rajʿ to mean rain.
TABRISI:86:9-17/r10.anchor: أي ذات المطر عن أكثر المفسرين

TABRISI:86:9-17/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:9-17/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:86:9-17/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets the sky's rajʿ as the sun, moon, and stars disappearing and then appearing again.
TABRISI:86:9-17/r11.anchor: يعني بالرجع شمسها وقمرها ونجومها تغيب ثم تطلع عن ابن زيد

TABRISI:86:9-17/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:86:9-17/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:86:9-17/r12.claim: Another view takes the sky's rajʿ as its repeated provision of good over time, including rain and people's sustenance.
TABRISI:86:9-17/r12.anchor: وقيل: رجع السماء إعطاؤها الخير الذي يكون من جهتها حالا بعد حال على مرور الأزمان فترجع بالغيث وأرزاق العباد وغير ذلك

THALABI:v10p180#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p180#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p180#2/r2.claim: The sky repeatedly brings rain and people’s sustenance each year; without it, people and their livelihoods would perish.
THALABI:v10p180#2/r2.anchor: والسماء ذات الرجع أي ترجع بالغيث وأرزاق العباد كل عام، لولا ذلك لهلكوا وهلكت معايشهم

THALABI:v10p180#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p180#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v10p180#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the sky’s “return” as clouds containing rain, and elsewhere simply as rain.
THALABI:v10p180#2/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس والسماء ذات الرجع قال: ذات المطر.

THALABI:v10p180#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p180#2/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v10p180#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الرجع الماء، وأنشد المنحل الهذلي في صفة السيف

THALABI:v10p180#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p180#2/r5.speaker: المنخل الهذلي
THALABI:v10p180#2/r5.claim: Al-Munakhkhal al-Hudhali’s sword poem uses “al-rajʿ” for rainwater, supporting the gloss “water.”
THALABI:v10p180#2/r5.anchor: وأنشد المنحل الهذلي في صفة السيف: أبيض كالرجع رسوب إذا … ما ثاج في محتفل يختلي

THALABI:v10p180#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p180#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p180#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd explains recurrence as the sun and moon setting and rising.
THALABI:v10p180#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: يعني بالرجع أن شمسها وقمرها يغيب ويطلع

BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r12.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r12.claim: Dhāt is feminine and means “possessor of”; rajʿ here means rain.
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r12.anchor: {والسماء ذات الرجع} ذات مؤنث ذو بمعنى الصاحب والرجع المطر

BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r13.speaker: العرب
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r13.claim: The Arabs reportedly called rain a return because they believed clouds carried water from the earth’s seas and returned it to the land.
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r13.anchor: سمى رجعا لما إن العرب كانوا يزعمون إن السحاب يحمل الماء من بحار الأرض ثم يرجعه إلى الأرض

BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r14.speaker: بعض العلماء
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r14.claim: Some scholars say the name expresses a hopeful wish that rain return; on this view rajʿ is a verbal noun of intransitive returning, not transitive causing return.
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r14.anchor: التفاؤل ليرجع ولذلك سموه أو باليؤوب فيكون الرجع مصدرا من اللازم بمعنى الرجوع لا من المتعدي قاله بعض العلماء

BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r15.claim: Rain is also called return because God brings it back repeatedly after creating it.
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r15.anchor: أو لأن الله يرجعه وقتا فوقتا بعد إيجاده وإحداثه

BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r16.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r16.claim: Al-Rāghib explains the name by the air returning the water it had taken.
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r16.anchor: وقال الراغب سمى المطر رجعا لرد الهواء ما تناوله من الماء

BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r17.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r17.claim: Kashf al-asrār says rain is a return because it comes back each year and recurs.
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r17.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" لأنه يرجع كل عام ويتكرر

BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r18.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r18.speaker: عبد القاهر الجرجاني
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r18.claim: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī explains the sky’s “return” by the sun and moon setting and rising and some stars moving retrograde.
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r18.anchor: وقال عبد القاهر الجرجاني في كتاب إعجاز القرآن إنما قال للسماء ذات الرجع لأن شمسها وقمرها يغيب ويطلع وبعض نجومها يرجع

BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r21.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r21.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r21.claim: The sky with its return signifies a father, the earth opening signifies a mother, and what grows from the earth signifies their child.
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r21.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن السماء ذات الرجع كالأب والأرض ذات الصدع كالأم وما ينبت من الأرض كالولد

BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r22.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r22.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r22.claim: The repeated oaths, first by the sky and then by sky and earth with their descriptions, signal abundant benefits and display their perfect knowledge and power.
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r22.anchor: أقسم الله بالسماء أو لا مجردة عن التوصيف وثانيا مقيدة بكونها ذات الرجع وكذا بالأرض ذات الصدع إيماء إلى المنة عليهم بكثرة المنافع ودلالة على العلم التام والقدرة الكاملة فيهما

BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r23.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r23.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r23.claim: The spirit’s sky has its return in the second creation; the body’s earth splits when separating from the spirit at death, or after their connection.
BURSEVI:v10p309#3/r23.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى سماء الروح ذات الرجع في النشأة الثانية وأرض البدن ذات الصدع بالانشقاق عن الروح وقت زهوقه أو الشق بعد اتصاله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says al-rajʿ means water in Arabic and cites a Hudhalī poet's comparison of a sword to al-rajʿ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r1.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الرجع في كلام العرب: الماء، وأنشد للهذلي يصف السيف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the sky begins with rain and brings it back every year.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: تبتدئ بالمطر، ثم ترجع به في كل عام (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r3.claim: Abū Isḥāq defines al-rajʿ as rain because it comes, returns, and recurs.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحق: الرجع: المطر؛ لأنه يجيء ويرجع ويتكرر (¬5) (¬6)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r4.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in ʿAṭāʾ's transmission, says rain begins and then returns every year.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r4.anchor: وهذا معنى قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء، قال: يبتدي بالمطر، ثم يرجع به في كل عام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r5.speaker: مقاتل وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة عن ابن عباس ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r5.claim: Muqātil, Saʿīd b. Jubayr, ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās, and Mujāhid describe a sky that rains, rains again, and returns to rain after each rainfall.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r5.anchor: وهو قول مقاتل (¬1)، وسعيد (بن جبير (¬2)، وعكرمة عن ابن عباس (¬3)) (¬4)، ومجاهد (¬5) قالوا: ذات المطر تمطر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r6.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r6.claim: The scholars of meaning say the sky repeatedly gives its good over time, returning it again and again.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r6.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: رجع السماء إعطاء الخير الذي يكون من جهتها حالا بعد حال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says the sky's return is the sun and moon reappearing after their setting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: هو أنها ترد وترجع شمسها وقمرها بعد مغيبهما (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r8.claim: Al-Wāḥidī prefers the first explanation: al-rajʿ is recurring rain.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p417/r8.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: هو أنها ترد وترجع شمسها وقمرها بعد مغيبهما (¬7)، والقول هو الأول (¬8)

QASHANI:86:11-14/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:86:11-14/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:86:11-14/r1.claim: The sky that returns signifies the spirit's return in the second creation.
QASHANI:86:11-14/r1.anchor: الروح ذات الرجع في النشأة الثانية

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r1.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r1.claim: Beyzāwī takes the return as the heaven's return to the position from which it moved in each cycle.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r1.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî gibi bazıları bundan semânın her devresinde hareket ettiği mevzi‘e rücû‘u mânasına olabileceğini söylemiş

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r2.claim: Elmalılı rejects literal motion of the heaven or celestial spheres: there is no proof for it, and the old astronomy is not established; transmitted exegesis concerns cycles within heaven.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r2.anchor: bizzat semânın kendisi, felekleri hareket ettiğine dair bir delil mâlum olmadığı ve eflâkin harekâtı hakkındaki eski hey’et nazariyeleri sâbit görülmediği cihetle

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r3.speaker: İbn Zeyd
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says the familiar heaven is meant, and its return is the sun, moon, and stars passing from state to state and station to station.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r3.anchor: İbn Zeyd’den menkul olan semâ, mâruf semâdır. Rec‘i de Şems ü Kamer’in ve kevâkibin hâlden hâle ve menzileden menzileye rücû‘udur

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r4.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the heaven as a rain-bearing cloud.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r4.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan mervî olan da yağmurlu bulut سَحَابٌ فِيهِ الْمَطَرُ diye tefsirdir

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r5.claim: Elmalılı cites al-Khansāʾ's verse as an image of repeated rain from a dark cloud coming at night.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r5.anchor: Vedâ günü öyle akan gözyaşları görürsün ki geceleyin gelip kaplayan ve mütemâdiyen yağdıran kara buluttaki rec‘e

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r6.claim: Elmalılı cites a verse by al-Huḏalī describing a sword as evidence for Arabic use of rajʿ for rain or water.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r6.anchor: beytinde geldiği vechile Arapça’da rec‘in yağmur ve su mânasına isti‘mâli müte‘âreftir

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r7.speaker: Zeccâc ve sâir eimme-i lügat
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r7.claim: They regard rajʿ for rain as metaphorical, deriving it from repeated sound, hoped-for return, annual sustenance, or water vapor returned by the sky to earth.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r7.anchor: Zeccâc ve sâir eimme-i lügatın beyânına göre “rec‘”in yağmura ıtlâkı vaz‘î bir isim olarak değil, mecazdır

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r8.claim: Elmalılı notes that al-Qāmūs also applies rajʿ to a lake, a place where water eddies, benefit, and spring vegetation.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r8.anchor: Kāmûs’ta mezkur olduğuna göre göle ve suyun anafor yaptığı su durağı yere ve menfaat ve fâideye ve baharda biten nebâta dahi ıtlak olunur

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r9.claim: Most exegetes take rajʿ as rain; on that reading, heaven can mean the familiar sky, while it may also mean cloud.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r9.anchor: Bundan dolayı ekser müfessirîn burada “rec‘”i yağmur diye tefsir etmişlerdir. Bu surette “semâ” mâruf mânasına olabileceği gibi

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r10.speaker: Mücâhid
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r10.claim: Mujāhid is cited for understanding samāʾ here as cloud.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r10.anchor: Bu surette “semâ” mâruf mânasına olabileceği gibi Mücâhid’den mervî olduğu üzere bulut

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r11.claim: On the rain reading, the verse means either a sky that repeatedly sends rain or a cloud from which rain repeatedly falls.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r11.anchor: Şu hâlde meâli: Döndürüp döndürüp yağmur yağdıran semâ, yahut dönüp dönüp yağan bulut demek olur

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r12.claim: Taking rajʿ as rain echoes the earlier mention of effused water in human creation through matching related terms.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r12.anchor: hilkat-i insanda zikri geçen mâ-i dâfik meselesine nazaran bir nevi mürâ‘ât-ı nazîr

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r13.speaker: Hasan
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r13.claim: Hasan explains rajʿ as rain and provision, since provision returns each year; this also encompasses water, plants, and benefit.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r13.anchor: Hasan’dan rivayette de “yağmur ve rızık, çünkü her sene döner rızık getirir” denilmiştir

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r14.claim: Some interpreters understand rajʿ as angels returning with human deeds; Elmalılı finds it apt to consider the angelic powers whose effects appear in recurring events.

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r15.claim: The context links every reading of rajʿ to return and restoration on the Day secrets are tested, affirming the resurrection already stated in 86:8.

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r16.claim: Elmalılı synthesizes the readings as a broad heavenly process of return and restoration, including celestial cycles, sunrise and sunset, winds and clouds, and cycles of light, darkness, heat, cold, moisture, and dryness.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r16.anchor: bütün bu tefsirlere şâmil semâvî bir fiil ve tesir mânası kasdedilmekle hepsi tevfik edilmiş ve bu ihtilâflar kesilmiş olur

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r20.claim: All three readings make the earth's crack a response to effects exerted upon it, complementing heaven's returning action from above.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r20.anchor: üç mânanın üçünde de Arz’ın sad‘ı, çatlayışı üzerinde icrâ olunan te’sîrâta bir infi‘al ve mutâva‘at mânası ifade etmekte birleşir

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r21.claim: Heaven's action and earth's receptivity are like a complementary pair that brings forth human life; humanity then returns to the hereafter, all under God's creative and preserving power.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r21.anchor: semâ ve Arz rec‘u sad‘ında biri diğerini derâguş ederek telkih eden zevceyn mesabesinde olup bunlar arasından tevellüd etmiş olan insanın yine bunlar arasından

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r22.claim: Some Sufis call the heavens fathers and the earthly realms mothers, extending the complementary-pair image.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r22.anchor: Bundan dolayı sûfiyyeden bazıları semâvâta “âbâ” ve arziyyâta “ümmehât” tâbir etmişlerdir

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r23.claim: If rajʿ is rain and sadʿ vegetation, rain fertilizing earth parallels effused water fertilizing a seed, suggesting that life is created by God's act; Elmalılı cites 36:36.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r23.anchor: “rec‘”i yağmur, “sad‘”ı nebat diye mülâhaza ettiğimiz takdirde

ELMALILI:86:11-17/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r24.claim: In summary, heaven manifests return and turning from above, while earth manifests fissuring and receptivity below, displaying capacity for becoming and decay.
ELMALILI:86:11-17/r24.anchor: yukarıdan icrâ-yı tesir eden bir ircâ‘, bir döndürüş ve çeviriş tecelliyâtı, aşağıda bir çatlayış bir teessür ve mutâva‘atla kevn ü fesâda kābiliyet tezâhürâtı bulunduğu muhakkaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r1.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r1.claim: One interpretation of the sky’s “return” is rain or rain-bearing clouds: the sky takes up earthly water as vapor, turns it into rain, and returns it, in a recurring cycle.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r1.anchor: a) “Yağmur veya yağmur yüklü bulutları olan” demektir. Buna göre “dönüşlü sema” ibaresi, göğün buharlaşma yoluyla yerden aldığı suları yağmura çevirip yere geri döndürmesini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r2.speaker: İbn Kesîr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r2.claim: Another interpretation refers to stars, the sun, and the moon repeatedly setting and rising.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r2.anchor: b) Gökte bulunan yıldızlar, güneş ve ayın tekrar tekrar batıp doğmalarını anlatır (İbn Kesîr, VIII, 397)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r3.claim: The Turkish translation adopts the interpretation about the recurring setting and rising of stars, the sun, and the moon.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r5.claim: By swearing by the sky and earth where these majestic events occur, the passage teaches that just as they are real manifestations of God’s power, the Qur’an is true and manifests His attribute of speech.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:86:11/r5.anchor: Âyetlerde bu muhteşem olayların gerçekleştiği gök ve yere yemin edilerek bunlar nasıl gerçek ise ve yüce Allah’ın kudretinin tecellileri ise Kur’an’ın da aynı şekilde gerçek olduğu, Allah’ın kelâm sıfatının tecellisi olduğu anlatılmaktadır

TUSTARI:86:11/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:86:11/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:86:11/r1.claim: Outwardly, the heaven is described as returning rain repeatedly.
TUSTARI:86:11/r1.anchor: قال: ظاهرها ذات الرجع بالمطر بعد المطر

FARRA:v3p254#2/r13.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p254#2/r13.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p254#2/r13.claim: The sky begins with rain and then brings it back each year.
FARRA:v3p254#2/r13.anchor: تبتدئ بالمطر، ثم ترجع به في كل عام

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p523#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p523#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p523#6/r1.claim: Al-rajʿ means rain; a Hudhalī poet comparing a sword to al-rajʿ uses the word for water.

NAHHAS:v5p199/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p199/r10.speaker: أهل التفسير
NAHHAS:v5p199/r10.claim: Commentators generally identify the sky’s رجع as rain, which returns year after year.
NAHHAS:v5p199/r10.anchor: قال أبو جعفر أهل التفسير على أنه المطر لأنه يرجع كل عام

NAHHAS:v5p199/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p199/r11.speaker: ابن زيد
NAHHAS:v5p199/r11.claim: Ibn Zayd instead identifies the رجع with the sun, moon, and stars.
NAHHAS:v5p199/r11.anchor: إلا ابن زيد فإنه قال ( والسماء ذات الرجع ) شمسها وقمرها ونجومها

NAHHAS:v5p199/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p199/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p199/r12.claim: رجعان is an attested, non-analogical plural of رجع; a regular analogy would give أرجع or رجوع.
NAHHAS:v5p199/r12.anchor: وجمع رجع رجعان سماع من العرب على غير قياس ولو قيس لقيل أرجع ورجوع

SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r1.claim: One interpretation takes الرجع as a verbal noun for the return of the sun and moon to the sky.
SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r1.anchor: قيل: هو مصدر بمعنى: رجوع الشمس والقمر إليها

SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r2.claim: Another interpretation is rain; an anonymous poetic description of a sword uses الرجع as its comparison.
SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r2.anchor: وقيل: المطر كقوله يصف سيفا: 4545 أبيض كالرجع رسوب إذا

SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r3.claim: A second cited poem calls rain الأوب, another name for it, alongside clouds and rain in its vocabulary.
SAMIN-DURR:86:11/r3.anchor: كما سمي أوبا كقوله: 4546 رباء شماء لا يأوي لقلتها إلا السحاب وإلا الأوب والسبل

ZAJJAJ:v5p312/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p312/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p312/r1.claim: The sky is described as having recurring rain, which comes back repeatedly.
ZAJJAJ:v5p312/r1.anchor: (ذات الرجع) ذات المطر لأنه يجيء ويرجع ويتكرر

ZAJJAJ:v5p312/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p312/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ZAJJAJ:v5p312/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda glosses rajʿ as water and cites al-Munkhal al-Hudhalī's word al-rajʿ to compare a sword's whiteness to water.
ZAJJAJ:v5p312/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الرجع: الماء، وأنشد بيت

ASAD-NOTES:86:8#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:86:8#n4/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:86:8#n4/r1.claim: Asad expands the call to consider the returning sky and splitting earth as a way to grasp God's creative and re-creative power more fully.
ASAD-NOTES:86:8#n4/r1.anchor: And, finally, in order to grasp more fully God's power of creation and re-creation, consider

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r2.claim: Khashya differs from fear because it arises from certain knowledge of the greatness of the one feared; fear may instead arise from coercion or terror.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r2.anchor: وتفترق الخشية عن الخوف، بأنها تكون عن يقين صادق بعظمة من نخشاه،

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r3.claim: Khushu differs from khudu: humility is a sincere response to majesty, while submission may be feigned from hypocrisy or fear, and Arabs speak of a humble heart but only figuratively of submission.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r3.anchor: كما يفترق الخشوع عن الخضوع، بأننا لا نخشع إلا عن إنفعال صادق بجلال مَن نخشع له.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r4.claim: All forms of khashya occur in worldly life, the arena of trial; its feared objects include the unseen, the Hour, the Last Day, hardship, poverty, orphan loss, and tyrannical wrongdoing.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r4.anchor: كل خشية فيه، على اختلاف صيغها، لا تكون إلا في الحياة الدنيا، لا في الآخرة، إذ الدنيا هي مجال الإبتلاء:

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r5.claim: When khashya is directed to a person or being rather than an event, Quran directs it to God alone, never to a creature.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p226/r5.anchor: وأما إذا تعلقت بذات، لا بأمر، فإنها في تقدير القرآن، لا تكون إلا الخشية لله، وحده، دون أي مخلوق.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r1.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r1.claim: Al-Rāghib restricts awb to voluntary return by a living creature; maʾāb is its verbal noun, and awwāb returns to God through repentance and obedience.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r1.anchor: لحظ الراغب أن الأوب ضرب من الرجوع وذلك أن الأوب لا يقال إلا في الحيوان الذي له إرادة، والمآب مصدر منه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r2.claim: The Qur’anic contexts generally use iyāb and maʾāb for creatures, while rujūʿ is usually predicated of them, with several exceptions for affairs returning to God.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r2.anchor: فيؤنس إلى قريب مما لحظه الراغب، حيث يأتي الإياب والمآب للخلق، وأما الرجوع فيأتي الفعل غالباً مسنداً إليهم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r3.speaker: الأصمعي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r3.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī interpreted iyāb in poetry as return at night, adducing a verse about a night-onset illness.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r3.anchor: كان الأصمعي يفسر الشعر الذي فيه ذكرُ الإياب أنه مع الليل، ويحتج بقوله

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم السجستاني
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r4.claim: Abū Ḥātim counters that iyāb means return at any time, citing a traveler, poetry, and Qur’an 88:25; he concedes the usage is often nocturnal.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r4.anchor: قال أبو حاتم، مستدركاً: ولكن أكثر ما يجئ على ما قال، رحمنا الله وإياه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r5.speaker: ابن فارس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r5.claim: Ibn Fāris says the root r-j-ʿ denotes return and repetition, and explains al-rajʿ as rain because the sky gives rain and returns to give it again.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r5.anchor: فعند ابن فارس أن الراء والجيم والعين أصل كبير مطَّرد منقاس يدل على ردّ وتكرار.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r6.speaker: أبو هلال العسكري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r6.claim: Abū Hilāl al-ʿAskarī distinguishes rujūʿ from iyāb: iyāb is return to the intended endpoint, as in 88:25.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r6.anchor: وأبو هلال العسكري، فرّق بين الرجوع والإياب، بأن الإياب هو الرجوع إلى منتهى القصد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r7.claim: The author suggests this semantic distinction may have informed Nāfiʿ’s question about iyāb, implying that it is not simply synonymous with rujūʿ.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p471/r7.anchor: فلعل هذا الفرق في الدلالة، أحسَّه نافع في سؤاله عن الإياب، وليس مرادفا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r7.claim: Verses 11–14 invoke a general physical phenomenon to show that the threatened Judgement is certain, not jest, and that people should prepare for it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p261/r7.anchor: A general physical phenomenon is presented to argue that the Day of Judgement

NASHR:v2p131/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p131/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p131/r6.claim: Al-Kisāʾī is reported to stop with hāʾ on ذات الرجع and ذات الصدع, along with other phrases beginning ذات.
NASHR:v2p131/r6.anchor: ذكر صاحب الكافي، وصاحب الهداية الوقف على ذات بهجة، و " ذات الصدور " وشبهه عن الكسائي بالهاء

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p365#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p365#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p365#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the sky's “return” as rain.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p365#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ والسماء ذات الرجع ﴾ قال ذات المطر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p365#3/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p365#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p365#3/r3.claim: Qatāda says the sky returns rain each year.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p365#3/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ والسماء ذات الرجع ﴾ قال ترجع بالغيث كل عام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r15.claim: The second oath is by the sky, understood as the canopy, though it may mean clouds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452/r15.anchor: والسماء: أقسم ثانيا بالسماء وهي المظلة. قيل: ويحتمل أن يكون السحاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the clouds contain rain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r1.anchor: السحاب فيه المطر. وقال الحسن: ترجع بالرزق كل عام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the sky brings provisions back each year.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن: ترجع بالرزق كل عام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd takes it as cyclical return of sun, moon, and stars between conditions and stations.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الرجع مصدر رجوع الشمس والقمر والكواكب من حال إلى حال ومن منزلة إلى منزلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r4.claim: The majority and standard linguistic view understand الرجع as rain, fitting the earth’s fissure producing vegetation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r4.anchor: والمشهور عند أهل اللغة وقول الجمهور: أن الرجع هو المطر، والصدع: ما تتصدع عنه الأرض من النبات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r5.claim: The Arabs supposedly imagined clouds carrying water from earthly seas and returning it to earth, naming it رجع or إرب in hope of return.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r5.anchor: تزعم العرب أن السحاب يحمل الماء من بحار الأرض ثم يرجعه إلى الأرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r6.speaker: الشاعر الهذلي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r6.claim: A Huthalī poet likens a white sword to rain, using الرجع for its whiteness and clarity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r6.anchor:
ومنه قول الهذلي:
أبيض كالرجع رسوب إذا ... ما ناح في محتفل يختلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r7.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r7.claim: A poet names clouds, rain, and إرب with words derived from return, illustrating source-noun naming.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r7.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
ربا شمالا يأوي لقلتها ... إلا السحاب وإلا الإرب والسبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r8.speaker: الخنساء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r8.claim: Al-Khansāʾ compares something to rain in a line using الرجع.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r8.anchor: قالت الخنساء: كالرجع في الموجنة السارية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r9.claim: Rain is called return because God brings it back repeatedly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: لأن الله تعالى يرجعه وقتا فوقتا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r10.claim: Another view says الرجع is angels, named for returning with people’s deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p452#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: الرجع: الملائكة، سموا بذلك لرجوعهم بأعمال العباد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r1.claim: The majority take the heaven in the oath to mean the canopy above us.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r1.anchor: والسماء وهي المظلة في قول الجمهور

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r2.claim: The majority explain al-rajʿ as rain, using a verbal noun of returning as a name for rainfall.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r2.anchor: وأصله مصدر رجع المعتدي واللازم أيضا في قول ومصدره الخاص به الرجوع

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r3.speaker: الخنساء
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r3.claim: Al-Khansa's comparison of flowing tears to rain in a dark rainy night supports rajʿ as rain.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r3.anchor: كما في قول الخنساء يوم الوداع ترى دموعا جارية كالرجع في المدجنة السارية

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r4.claim: The cited verse-like line also uses awb and sabl as names for rain, parallel to rajʿ.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r4.anchor: لا يأوى لقلتها إلا السحاب ولا الأوب والسبل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r5.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r5.claim: Some explain the rain as water taken up from the earth's seas and returned by clouds; Alusi says this rests on an assumption and deserves scrutiny.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r5.anchor: ليرجع أو لأن السحاب يحمله من بحار الأرض ثم يرجعه إلى الأرض وبنى هذا غير واحد على الزعم وفيه بحث

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r6.claim: Another explanation makes the referent clouds, which God sends back from time to time.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r6.anchor: وعن أو المراد به فيه النحل لأن الله تعالى يرجعه حينا فحينا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r7.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says the return brings sustenance each year, or that the wording expresses an optimistic expectation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن لأنه يرجع بالرزق كل عام أو أرادوا بذلك التفاؤل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid interpret heaven as clouds and al-rajʿ as rain.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r8.anchor: ابن عباس ومجاهد تفسير بالسحاب والرجع بالمطر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the heaven as the familiar sky and its return as the sun, moon, and stars passing from state to state and station to station.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r9.anchor: وقال ابن زيد السماء هي المعروفة والرجع رجحوع الشمس والقمر والكواكب من حال إلى حال ومن منزلة إلى منزلة فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r10.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r10.claim: A further view takes the return as the celestial sphere itself cycling back to its starting point, with its apogee and perigee exchanging positions.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r10.anchor: وقيل رجوعها نفسها فإنها ترجع في كل دورة إلى الموضع الذي تتحرك منه وهذا مبني على أن السماء والفلك واحد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r11.claim: Alusi says the apparent early Muslim view distinguishes heaven from the sphere and does not make it rotate; motion of the sphere belongs to philosophers and their followers.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r11.anchor: أن ظاهر كلام السلف أن السماء غير الفلك وإنها لا تدور ولا تتحرك والذي ذكر رأي الفلاسفة ومن تابعهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r12.claim: Some identify al-rajʿ as the angels, named for returning with the servants' deeds.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p99#3/r12.anchor: وقيل الرجع الملائكة عليهم السلام سموا بذلك لرجوعهم بأعمال العباد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p395/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p395/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p395/r2.claim: The sky's recurring return is rain, which comes back year after year.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p395/r2.anchor: أي ذات المطر لأنه يرجع كل عام ويتكرر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p395/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p395/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p395/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the returning thing as clouds that bring back rain.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p395/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هو السحاب يرجع بالمطر.

BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r2.claim: One view says the sky repeatedly returns to the place from which it moves in each cycle.
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r2.anchor: ترجع في كل دورة إلى الموضع الذي تتحرك عنه

BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r3.claim: Alternatively, al-rajʿ is rain, named for its repeated return at intervals.
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r3.anchor: وقيل الرجع المطر سمي به كما سمي أوبا لأن الله يرجعه وقتا فوقتا

BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r4.claim: Another explanation is that clouds carry water from the seas and return it to the earth; on this reading, sky may mean cloud.
BAYDAWI-FULL:86:10-16/r4.anchor: لما قيل من أن السحاب يحمل الماء من البحار ثم يرجعه إلى الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r5.claim: The preceding concise statements prove resurrection, requital, and divine oneness; this establishes the Quran as God's speech and all it says as true, prompting an oath to affirm its truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r5.anchor: فثبت أن القرآن كلام الله سبحانه وتعالى , فثبت أن كل ما فيه حق مع منازعتهم في ذلك كله , اقتضى الحال الإقسام على حقيته

BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r6.claim: The sky's return is its cyclical motion back to where it began.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r6.anchor: ذات الرجع * } التي ترجع بالدوران إلى الموضع الذي ابتدأت الدوران منه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r7.claim: The recurring return includes night and day, the sun, moon, stars, and the seasons with their changing weather.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r7.anchor: فترجع الأحوال التي كانت وتصرمت من الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر والكواكب والفصول من الشتاء وما فيه من برد ومطر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r8.claim: The return also includes vegetation after it has withered and become soil mixed with the earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r8.anchor: والنبات بعد تهشمه وصيرورته ترابا مختلطا بتراب الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r9.speaker: من يقول
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r9.claim: One reported explanation says clouds take water from the sea, rise, condense it in the air, and return it to earth.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r9.anchor: وترجع الماء على قول من يقول : إن السحاب يأخذه من البحر ويعلو به فيعصره في الهواء ثم يرده إلى الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r10.claim: These recurring processes conclusively show that their maker can restore anything that perishes exactly as it was.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390/r10.anchor: وغير ذلك من الأمور الدال كل منها قطعا على أن فاعل ذلك قادر على إعادة كل ما فني كما كان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r3.claim: Biqāʿī likens the upper world to a man and the lower world to a woman.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r3.anchor: فجمع بالقسم العالم العلوي الذي هو كالرجل والسفلي الذي هو كالمرأة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r4.claim: As a man waters a woman and she yields a child, heaven waters earth and it splits to yield vegetation.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r4.anchor: فكما أن الرجل يسقيها من مائه فتصدع عن الولد , فكذلك السماء تسقي الأرض فتتصدع عن النبات

BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r5.claim: As plants return after decay, people will return after death by their Lord's permission, with no difference between the two restorations.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p390#2/r5.anchor: بعد فنائه وصيرورته رفاتا فيعود كما كان فكذلك تتصدع عن الناس بعد فنائهم فيعودون كما كانوا بإذن ربها من غير فرق أصلا

DURR-FULL:v8p475/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r15.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sky’s recurring return is rain after rain.
DURR-FULL:v8p475/r15.anchor: أخرج عبد الرزاق والفريابي وعبد بن حميد والبخاري في تاريخه وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم والحاكم وصححه وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس في قوله: {والسماء ذات الرجع} قال: المطر بعد المطر

DURR-FULL:v8p477/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p477/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p477/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies al-rajʿ with clouds that rain and then return with rain.
DURR-FULL:v8p477/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد {والسماء ذات الرجع} قال: السحاب تمطر ثم ترجع بالمطر

DURR-FULL:v8p477/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p477/r3.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v8p477/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the sky returns rain each year.
DURR-FULL:v8p477/r3.anchor: عن عطاء {والسماء ذات الرجع} قال: ترجع بالمطر كل عام

DURR-FULL:v8p477/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p477/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p477/r7.claim: Qatāda says heaven returns people's provision each year; without it they and their livestock would perish.
DURR-FULL:v8p477/r7.anchor: عن قتادة {والسماء ذات الرجع} قال: ترجع إلى العباد برزقهم كل عام لولا ذلك لهلكوا وهلكت مواشيهم

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3415#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3415#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3415#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the sky’s rajʿ as rain followed by rain.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3415#3/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : والسماء ذات الرجع قال : المطر بعد المطر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r1.claim: The oath’s heaven may mean the familiar sky or the clouds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r1.anchor: السماء في هذا القسم يحتمل أن تكون المعروفة، ويحتمل أن تكون السحاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r2.claim: Al-rajʿ means rain and its water.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r3.speaker: الهذلي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r3.claim: A Hudhalī poetic line uses al-rajʿ for rain, describing it as white and descending.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r3.anchor: أبيض كالرجع رسوب إذا ... ما شاخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies al-rajʿ as clouds containing rain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: الرجع، السحاب فيه المطر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains the name by the clouds’ yearly return with sustenance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r5.anchor: قال الحسن: لأنه يرجع بالرزق كل عام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r6.speaker: غيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r6.claim: Another explanation says the rain is called al-rajʿ because it returns to the earth.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r6.anchor: قال غيره لأنه يرجع إلى الأرض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd takes al-rajʿ as the recurring motion of the sun, moon, and stars from one state to another, including a station they leave and revisit.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p466#2/r7.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: الرجع مصدر رجوع الشمس والقمر والكواكب من حال إلى حال، ومنه منزلة تذهب وترجع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p84#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p84#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p84#3/r1.claim: The sky's return is its rain; it is named for rain's repeated coming and return.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p84#3/r1.anchor: أي ذات المطر وسمي المطر رجعا لأنه يجيء ويرجع ويتكرر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says al-rajʿ means rain, and also describes it as the cloud containing rain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: الرجع: المطر. وعنه: هو السحاب فيه المطر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains the recurring return as the sky raining and then raining again.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r2.anchor: وعنه: {والسماء ذات الرجع} تمطر ثم تمطر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r3.claim: Qatada says the sky returns people’s provision every year; without this, people and their livestock would perish.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: ترجع رزق العباد كل عام، ولولا ذلك لهلكوا وهلكت مواشيهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the stars, sun, and moon return, coming from this direction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p376#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: ترجع نجومها وشمسها وقمرها، يأتين من هاهنا

JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r1.claim: Rajʿ comes from returning something repeatedly, state after state, or giving it again and again.
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r1.anchor: الرجع: أصله من الرجوع، وهو أن يرجع بالشيء حالا بعد حال، رجعته رجعا: إذا أعطيته مرة بعد مرة.

JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r8.claim: The oath may swear by the sky itself, honored for its importance in power and blessing, or by the Lord of the sky.
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r8.anchor: والسماء قيل: أقسم بنفس السماء العظيم موقعها في القدرة والنعمة. وقيل: برب السماء ذات الرجع

JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, and al-Dahhak explain the returning sky as rain that comes again and again.
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r9.anchor: قيل: ذات المطر الذي ترجع به حالا بعد حال، عن ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وقتادة، والضحاك.

JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd says the sun, moon, and stars set and then rise again.
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r10.anchor: وقيل: شمسها وقمرها ونجومها تغيب، ثم تطلع، عن ابن زيد.

JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r11.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas identifies the sky as clouds containing water, raining repeatedly as needed.
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: هي السحاب فيه الماء، عن ابن عباس. أي: تمطر حالا بعد حال، بحسب المصلحة.

JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r12.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r12.claim: A further explanation is rain that recurs more than once.
JISHUMI:v10p7367#2/r12.anchor: وقيل: الرجع هو المطر يأتي مرة بعد أخرى.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r1.claim: The sky’s returning quality is its rain, which returns every year.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r1.anchor: ذات المطر , لأنه يرجع في كل عام , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r2.claim: A second view takes the phrase as clouds because they return with rain.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r3.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r3.claim: The sky returns to the state it had before.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r3.anchor: ذات الرجوع إلى ما كانت , قاله عكرمة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r4.claim: The phrase can refer to the returning stars.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r4.anchor: ذات النجوم الراجعة , قاله ابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r5.claim: A further possibility is that it means angels who return to heaven with people’s deeds; this is an oath.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p248/r5.anchor: ذات الملائكة لرجوعهم إليها بأعمال العباد

MUJAHID:v2p750/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p750/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p750/r1.claim: Mujahid explains the heaven of return as bearing clouds: it rains, then returns with rain.
MUJAHID:v2p750/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ والسماء ذات الرجع ﴾ يعني ذات السحاب يقول تمطر ثم ترجع بالمطر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#7/r1.claim: The sky's “return” is rain, so named because it comes back each time.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p331#7/r1.anchor: أى المطر وسمى به لعوده كل حين

QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r1.speaker: عامة المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r1.claim: Most commentators understand the heaven's return as rain, which comes back each year with rain after rain.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r1.anchor: ترجع كل سنة بمطر بعد مطر. كذا قال عامة المفسرين.

QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r2.claim: Lexicographers define al-rajʿ as rain; al-Mutanakhil's sword simile is cited as evidence for this usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r2.anchor: وقال أهل اللغة: الرجع: المطر، وأنشدوا للمتنخل يصف سيفا شبهه بالماء

QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r3.speaker: المنخل
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r3.claim: Al-Mutanakhil likens a sword to rain, using al-rajʿ to convey its image and force.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r3.anchor: أنشدوا للمتنخل يصف سيفا شبهه بالماء: أبيض كالرجع رسوب إذا ما ثاخ في محتفل يختلي

QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r4.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r4.claim: Al-Khalīl says al-rajʿ means rain itself and can also mean spring vegetation.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r4.anchor: قال الخليل: الرجع: المطر نفسه، والرجع أيضا: نبات الربيع

QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r5.claim: An alternative takes the heaven possessing al-rajʿ to mean possessing benefit.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r5.anchor: وقيل: { ذات الرجع }: أي ذات النفع.

QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r6.claim: Rain is also called awb, just as it is called rajʿ; a poem illustrates the usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r6.anchor: وقد يسمى المطر أيضا أوبا، كما يسمى رجعا، قال: رباء شماء لا يأوي لقلتها إلا السحاب وإلا الأوب والسبل

QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r7.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r7.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says the sun, moon, and stars return across the sky, rising in one direction and setting in another.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r7.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: الشمس والقمر والنجوم يرجعن في السماء تطلع من ناحية وتغيب في أخرى

QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r8.claim: Another view identifies the returning ones as angels who go back to heaven with people's deeds.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r8.anchor: وقيل: ذات الملائكة لرجوعهم إليها بأعمال العباد

QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r9.claim: The heaven is an oath, and the earth is a second oath.
QURTUBI-FULL:86:11-14/r9.anchor: وهذا قسم. { والأرض ذات الصدع } قسم آخر

QUTB-ZILAL:86:11/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:11/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:11/r1.claim: Because some doubt may remain that the promised event must occur, God states the decisive truth categorically and links it to cosmic scenes as at the sūra's opening.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:11/r1.anchor: يربط بين هذا القول وبين مشاهد الكون

QUTB-ZILAL:86:11/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:11/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:11/r2.claim: Al-rajʿ is rain, which the sky sends back repeatedly.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:11/r2.anchor: والرجع المطر ترجع به السماء مرة بعد مرة

QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r2.claim: Rain flowing from heaven and vegetation emerging from earth portray plant life beginning, like flowing reproductive fluid and an embryo emerging from the darkness of the womb.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r2.anchor: أشبه شيء بالماء الدافق من الصلب والترائب  ؛  والجنين المنبثق من ظلمات الرحم

QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r3.claim: The shared life, scene, and motion reveal a stable order and crafted work pointing to a maker unlike anything else in the nature or outward form of his work.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r3.anchor: الذي لا يشبهه أحد لا في حقيقة الصنعة ولا في شكلها الظاهر

QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r5.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r5.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r5.claim: God swears by these two created things and events; their scenes, implications, and the expression's sound convey force, penetration, and decisiveness.
QUTB-ZILAL:86:12/r5.anchor: يقسم الله بهذين الكائنين وهذين الحدثين
